paragraphs: Rav Huna of Tzippori, Rabbi Yose of Mada, and Rav Avira before Rabbi Rabbah; Rashi explains: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. Yuchasin objects to him (see Rabbi Avira). At the end of Rosh Hashanah, 34, end of side b, the reading before us there is Rav Chana of Tzippori. It appears that he was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, since there he says in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. In that matter in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Rosh Hashanah: Rabbi Chuna Rabbah of Tzippori, in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. In Jerusalem Talmud, end of Berakhot chapter 4: Rav Huna Rubba of Tzippori, in Rav Yochanan’s name. In Shekalim chapter 1: Rabbi Chuna Rabbah of Tzippori, in Rabbi Chiyya Rabba’s name. Yuchasin writes: R.Ch. of Tzippori, Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Tamid Nishchat; I did not find it. In chapter Kelal Gadol, halakhah 2: Rabbi Chanina in Rabbi Abbahu’s name. In Nedarim chapter 9, halakhah 1: R.Ch. of Tzippori in Rabbi Pinchas’s name. In Babylonian Talmud, Yoma, “77, ס, side b” [locator as printed], Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Huna of Tzippori’s name; in Midrash Kohelet, Rabbi Pinchas in Rabbi Chanin of Tzippori’s name; in Tanchuma Tetzaveh, Rav Huna of Tzippori; at the end of Eikhah’s opening exposition, Rav Huna Rabbah of Tzippori. In Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit chapter 2, halakhah 2: Rav Acha bar Yitzchak in Rabbi Chuna Rubba of Tzippori’s name. In Berakhot chapter 4, mishnah 3, that matter is in Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori’s name. Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori objects to Rabbi Immi: Orlah chapter 3, halakhah 2. Chananya ben Akhbari performed work for him. Rabbi Yochanan of Tzippori: Midrash Chazit, on “His head is finest gold”; that matter in Vayikra Rabbah chapter 19 has Rabbi Chanin of Tzippori. In Jerusalem Talmud, Kiddushin chapter 1, halakhah 1: Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi; Rabbi Chanun in Rabbi Chuna Rubba of Tzippori’s name …; Rabbi Yochanan of Tzippori; Rabbi Acha; Rabbi Chinena in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name.
